description: 12V to 5V switching regulator module
notes: 3-pin SIP on a 7805 footprint - no inductor, no feedback network, no layout risk. ONE: the one dev board, the 8x8 matrix and the level shifter (ADR 0015 - there is no display board). Its share of the clamp-legal worst case is 68-78% of 1A (power-entry-instrument.md). IT IS 10.4mm TALL UPRIGHT, which fits anywhere on the main board, under the key boards included (mechanical/drc.echo 'main board parts room under the key boards' and 'regulator block fits where it stands') - no need to lay it flat. *** MINIMUM INPUT IS 8V FOR THE 5.0V PART, NOT THE 7V ON THE FEATURES LINE - THAT 7V IS THE 3.3V PART'S. *** The front page says 'Wide input range (7V - 28V)' and the selection table says R-78E3.3-1.0 = 7-28, R-78E5.0-1.0 = 8-28. Not binding here - worst case at the buck input is ~10.96V (rack at 11.4V, less ~0.28V of Schottky, ~36mV of R-ILIM and FET, ~121mV in 4m of Cat5 at 360mA), so ~3V of margin and even a 20% rack sag clears it - but anyone sizing the umbilical against '7V' is working to the wrong part. DERATING: 100% of rated load from -40C to +60C ambient, then linear to 60% at +85C with a hard cutoff, natural convection. At 65C ambient that permits 92% against the 69-78% actually drawn, ~14 points of margin, and 78% stays legal to ~73.8C. SWITCHING FREQUENCY 330kHz for the 3.3V and 5V outputs (570kHz for 12V) - the figure C-AA-ADC is sized against. Max capacitive load 220uF. No minimum load on the 5V part. Short-circuit protection is CONTINUOUS WITH AUTOMATIC RECOVERY, not latching. BUY RECOM'S OWN, FROM A DISTRIBUTOR: DigiKey 945-2201-ND, Active, 13,971 at $4.51 [web https://www.digikey.com/en/products/result?keywords=R-78E5.0-1.0, 2026-10-03]; Newark 1,718, Sager 4,951 [web https://www.findchips.com/search/R-78E5.0-1.0, 2026-10-03]. NOT FROM LCSC OR JLC: RECOM's own listing there (C3033024) holds 0, and what is in stock under the same name is other makers' (YLPTEC C22371890, EVISUN C53159158 on 2026-10-03) - other makers' parts sold there switch at 520-850 kHz, not 330 kHz [web LCSC listings, 2026-09-29], and C-AA-ADC is sized against 330 kHz. So the sheet carries no LCSC number for it. Hand-soldered (THT), then ITS PINS CUT to config/body.yaml boards.tht_trim below the board: as supplied they do not clear the oak through the bottom plate's window (mechanical/drc.echo 'through-hole tails under the main board clear of the bottom plate'). Cut after soldering, with flush cutters, leaving the tail visible in its fillet

description: Bulk at the LED row's 12V feed point
notes: Bulk belongs at the load: the row's PWM steps its whole current at once, and a ferrite is a wire at that rate. ONE, at the row's feed end on the main board, where the 12V from J-UMB reaches it, the 100 nF at each LED (C-LED) taking the edges (ADR 0028). UCW1E471MNL1GS (LCSC C340751): 25 V on the 12 V feed

description: LC between the umbilical node and the buck input
notes: A real inductor, not a bead. SWPA6028S220MT (LCSC C51349), 22 uH: the value the input LC's derivation uses (power-entry-instrument.md)

description: ORs USB VBUS with the umbilical-derived 5V rail for bench use
notes: One diode from the buck into the dev board's 5V node, which USB VBUS also feeds. Bench affordance for E5, explicitly not a standalone mode. SS14-E3/61T (LCSC C47460): SMA like D-REVSHUNT's SMC, so machine-placed with no hand step, and 2.29 max high [ds SS14.pdf p.3], inside the main board's SMD height. VF 0.50 V max at 1 A [ds p.2]; at 0.7-0.8 A it drops about 0.45 V, leaving about 4.55 V at the dev board's 5V pin - fine for its 3V3 LDO [calc]. Dissipation 0.78 A x 0.45 V = 0.35 W, +31 C at RthJA 88 C/W [calc, ds p.2]. The breath sensor is not on this rail

description: Bulk cap at the umbilical entry / buck input - the C of L-BUCK-IN's LC
notes: Completes the LC: L-BUCK-IN had an L and no C. One buck and one capacitor. Also the capacitance the module load switch's inrush ramp is sized against (ADR 0005). 25V part on a 12V rail for derating. UCM1E101MCL1GS (LCSC C729678): AN ELECTROLYTIC, NEVER A CERAMIC - its ESR is the LC's damping (power-entry-instrument.md, the input LC)

description: TVS across the umbilical power pair at the instrument
notes: 15V standoff on a 12V rail. The power pair is the one the old 6-channel array could never have covered - six channels against eight conductors, and the six non-power ones are the natural fit

description: Shunt diode across the umbilical power pair at the instrument
notes: UNRETROFITTABLE. A rollover/console RJ45 lead swaps 3 and 6, which on the T568B map are +12V and PWR_GND - reverse polarity into the instrument, from a consumable patch lead that looks identical to a good one. Cathode to the +12V pin: reversed, it conducts hard, the module's LT1641-1 sees a short and LATCHES OFF, and the panel LED says so - the load switch becomes the fuse. *** PACKAGE IS DO-214AB (SMC), NOT DO-214AC *** [SS34.pdf p.1, 'MECHANICAL DATA / Case: SMC (DO-214AB)']. DO-214AC is the SS14's package, and the two are a footprint apart on unretrofittable reverse-polarity protection sitting on the +12V pin - check it against the drawing before the board goes out

description: The analog star's single tie: AGND_INST to PWR_GND at one point
notes: COPPER, NOT A PART: nothing is bought or placed. The one place AGND_INST (an island on layer 2) meets the PWR_GND plane, under U-ADC between its VSS and its digital pins, so the ADC's SPI edges return straight into the plane (power-entry-instrument.md section 2). The net tie lets KiCad's DRC allow that join there and nowhere else. Assembly: none

description: P-channel hot-plug inrush limiter between J-UMB's +12V and the instrument's bulk
notes: SOURCE AT THE CONNECTOR, DRAIN TO THE BULK: the body diode must point back at J-UMB, or a plug-in charges C-STRIP-BULK and C-BUCK-IN through it at whatever the cable allows. Its Miller ramp is what keeps U-ISO under its over-current threshold on a hot-plug (hotplug-iso-ocp, power-entry-instrument.md 'Hot-plug inrush'). -30 V, V_GS +/-12 V max, R_DS(on) 60 mohm max at -4.5 V, V_GS(th) -0.5/-0.9/-1.3 V [ds AOS-AO3401A.pdf p.1-2]: the 1:1 gate divider holds it at half the input, -5.9 V at 11.8 V. The ramp is ~0.23 A for ~50 ms, 1.7 W peak and ~85 mJ in the FET: its single-pulse rating at 50 ms is ~12 W and Z_th ~12 K/W [ds p.4 Figs 10-11, read off the curves], ~20 K. JLC basic part, LCSC C15127

description: Q-INRUSH gate to source (turn-off, and the top of its V_GS divider)
notes: With R-INRUSH-G a 1:1 divider: V_GS is half the input once on. 0805W8F1004T5E, LCSC C17514

description: Q-INRUSH gate to PWR_GND (turn-on; sets the ramp current through C-INRUSH-GD)
notes: The ramp is dV/dt = I / C-INRUSH-GD, I being (V_in - V_plateau)/R-INRUSH-G less V_plateau/R-INRUSH-GS, ~9 uA: ~400 V/s. 0805W8F1004T5E, LCSC C17514

description: Q-INRUSH gate to source: the gate follows the plug-in step
notes: KEEP IT AT LEAST 45x C-INRUSH-GD. The source jumps 12 V in microseconds when the plug makes contact; the gate follows through this and is held back by C-INRUSH-GD, so V_GS jumps by 12 V x C-GD/(C-GS + C-GD) = -0.26 V against a 0.5 V minimum threshold. A smaller value turns the FET on hard at every plug-in. CL21B105KBFNNNE, LCSC C28323

description: Q-INRUSH Miller capacitor, gate to drain through R-INRUSH-GD
notes: Sets the ramp: ~400 V/s, ~0.23 A into the instrument's ~570 uF, under the load switch's lowest limit with the loads added. X7R loses some capacitance at bias, which speeds the ramp a little. CL21B223KBANNNC, LCSC C1729

description: In series with C-INRUSH-GD: damps the connector node at plug-in
notes: With the FET off at plug-in, J-UMB's node is the cable's inductance into D-TVS-PWR's capacitance and the gate network: undamped it rings to twice the rail, past D-TVS-PWR's 15 V standoff. 22 ohm holds it under (sim/, hot-plug). 0805W8F220JT5E, LCSC C17561

description: Q-INRUSH gate reset, anode to PWR_GND, cathode to the gate
notes: After an unplug C-INRUSH-GS keeps V_GS while the instrument drains, leaving the gate below ground; this clamps it at about -0.4 V, so a plug-in once the input has fallen starts from off. A replug while the bulk still holds charge is not covered (sim/, replug). Silicon, not Schottky: a Schottky's leakage is comparable to the ~9 uA gate current. LCSC C81598

description: 5.000V precision series reference for the breath sensor supply
notes: The MPXV4006DP is ratiometric, so ITS SUPPLY IS ITS SCALE FACTOR - that is the whole reason for a separate reference here. Buffered by half of U-BUF, and see R-ISO-REF for the network that makes that buffer stable. THE HIGH GRADE, NO 'A' IN THE ORDER CODE: grade and accuracy are figures.yaml ref5050-grade, and are not restated here. The 'A' suffix is the WORSE (Standard) grade [ds REF5050.pdf SBOS410O Table 4-2 p.3], the opposite of what a reader expects from a letter suffix - do not let a substitution add it back. Same SOIC-8 and pinout for both grades [ds Table 5-1 p.4]. TI REF5050IDR, LCSC C24696, 4401 in stock at USD 1.92 (1-9) [web jlcpcb.com parts search 2026-09-30]. FETCH NOTE: ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ref5050.pdf is a 404 since rev O; the working URL is ti.com/lit/ds/sbos410/sbos410.pdf

description: Dual RRIO op-amp: breath buffer + reference buffer
notes: SOIC-8, and it RUNS ON +12V, NOT 5V: a +12V fault on the BREATH conductor is then at the rail, so there is no clamp current and the >=3.3k protection-resistor requirement goes away. Same part as the module op-amps - DEVICE FACTS ARE ON U-OPA-PITCH and are not repeated here. STABILITY IS THE WHOLE OF THIS ROW. The reference half drives the sensor's 100nF decoupler ALONE - C-REF-OUT is on the REF5050, not on this output (see figures.yaml cref-out-node). Against the specified 375 ohm open-loop Zo that is 1.5 degrees of phase margin as a bare follower, so IT MUST BE COMPENSATED, with TI's own dual-feedback network [SBOS737C Figure 56]: R-ISO-REF 37.4R, R-FB-REF 10k taken at VS, R-FBX-REF 100R + C-FB-REF 1nF at this pin. Its phase margin is figures.yaml riso-ref-phase-margin (sim/), AND the DC error across R-ISO-REF is exactly zero, so the 2% ratiometric objection to an out-of-loop resistor never has to be paid - see figures.yaml riso-ref-topology

description: Output and input capacitors on the REF5050
notes: REF5050 VIN bypass and REF5050 VOUT load capacitor - one each, with a 100nF from C-DECOUPLE-CARRIER alongside each. *** NEITHER IS ON THE BUFFER'S OUTPUT *** (see figures.yaml cref-out-node); this is the rail that IS the breath scale factor. The VOUT one is not a choice - the part cannot be built without it [SBOS410O 8.4.1 p.26: 'Confirm that a output capacitor (CL) is connected from VOUT to GND. For output stability, verify that the ESR value of CL less than or equal to 1.5 ohm', with Figure 8-6 giving CL = 1uF to 50uF] - and the other is the 8.4.1 supply bypass (1-10uF). 10uF on the buffer output would be 10000x the OPA2197's 1 nF capacitive-load limit. The REF5050 drives only the OPA2197's input bias current (+/-20 pA max at 25C), so its load regulation (20 ppm/mA typ, 30 max, 50 over temperature) contributes ZERO to the breath scale factor. NO SERIES RESISTOR, NO FOOTPRINT FOR ONE: the X7R goes straight from VOUT to AGND_INST. 8.4.1's 'ESR <= 1.5 ohm' is a stability ceiling an X7R meets, 9.4.1.1 p.29 says 'A resistor in series with the output capacitor is optional', and the 1-1.5 ohm TI recommends is 'for better noise performance' only - low ESR gain-peaks the reference's own noise [p.28]. That noise is 4.5 uVrms against a 1.46 mV ADC LSB (325x below), so even a 3x peak leaves it 108x below one LSB [calc], and the load is a constant pA, so there is no transient for peaking to ring on. The TRIM/NR 1uF is DECLINED for the same reason: 8.3.6 p.26 halves the same 4.5 uVrms and lengthens start-up. Samsung CL31B106KBHNNNE, LCSC C89632

description: Isolation resistor, reference buffer dual-feedback network (SBOS737C Fig. 56)
notes: OPA2197 output to U-BREATH VS (pin 2). One of four parts in TI's dual-feedback reference-buffer network [SBOS737C 8.2.3 p.30, Figure 56 'Precision Reference Buffer']; the other three are R-FB-REF, R-FBX-REF and C-FB-REF. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE. *** TI'S FIGURE TRANSFERS TO OUR 100 nF DESPITE ITS 10uF BECAUSE R_ISO IS SET BY Zo, NOT BY C_L *** - the attenuation R_ISO/(Zo+R_ISO) and the pole-zero ratio both depend only on R_ISO/Zo, and C_L moves both corners together and cancels. 37.4R is Zo/10 against the specified 375 ohm (see U-OPA-PITCH). Simulated margin: figures.yaml riso-ref-phase-margin (sim/, against TI's macromodel, which also reproduces Figure 56's published 89 degrees). *** DC ERROR ACROSS THIS RESISTOR IS EXACTLY ZERO BY TOPOLOGY *** - C-FB-REF blocks at DC so no current flows in R-FBX-REF, input current is pA so none flows in R-FB-REF, and the amplifier therefore forces V(VS) = 5.000 V. Its value and tolerance stop mattering; the 1% is bought for stock reasons. Power is (10mA)^2 x 37.4 = 3.74 mW in an 0805. DO NOT PUT R_ISO INSIDE THE LOOP: it buys nothing at ANY value - 1.5 degrees at 10R and 1.5 degrees at 37.4R, the same as fitting nothing. See figures.yaml riso-ref-topology

description: DC feedback resistor, reference buffer - taken at the sensor's VS pin
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | 10k is this board's value, not TI's scaled (Figure 56's are in figures.yaml riso-ref-topology). (1) The guaranteed-over-temperature I_B of 5 nA through 10k is 50 uV = 0.034 LSB on a rail that IS the ratiometric scale factor. (2) R_F x C_F sets the HANDOVER frequency above which the loop closes on the amplifier's own output instead of on VS; the sensor draws 10 mA, so above the handover any load-current change appears at VS across R-ISO-REF. 10k x 1nF puts it at 15.9 kHz, well above the 500 Hz channel, and |Z_out| at VS is then 1.20 ohm at 500 Hz (sim/ zout-as-netlisted)

description: AC feedback resistor, reference buffer - taken at the OPA2197 output pin
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | 1% of R-FB-REF, so that above the handover the loop closes on the amplifier output with only 1% of VS leaking in. R_Fx x C_F is 100 ns here against the 3.74 us TI's own rule (R_Fx C_F = R_ISO C_L) would give, and the simulation says it costs nothing - the binding condition is |R_Fx + 1/(2.pi.f C_F)| much less than R_F AT CROSSOVER (riso-ref-phase-margin): at 1.25 MHz |100 - j127| = 162 ohm against 10k, a 62x margin

description: AC feedback capacitor, reference buffer
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | C0G, because this capacitor sets the handover frequency and an X7R's DC-bias and temperature derating would move it. 1nF at R-FB-REF's 10k gives a 15.9 kHz handover. IT IS ALSO WHY THE DC ERROR IS ZERO: blocking at DC is what leaves R-FB-REF as the only feedback path, so the amplifier servos the SENSOR pin rather than its own output. NOTE FOR THE SPICE DECK: this network leaves the summing node with no DC path except through R-FB-REF, so a simulator needs a leak resistor there for convergence and a real board does not - the amplifier's input leakage provides it

description: Series resistor ahead of the REF5050 input, into the zener clamp
notes: +12V to REF_VIN. THE RAIL'S TVS DOES NOT PROTECT THE REFERENCE: D-TVS-PWR clamps at up to 24.4 V [ds LITTELFUSE-SMAJ-SERIES-SMAJ15A.pdf p.2] and the REF5050's VIN abs max is 18 V [ds REF5050.pdf p.5]. This resistor limits the zener's current to (24.4 - 15.75)/330 = 26 mA [calc]. DC drop at the reference's 1.2 mA max [ds REF5050.pdf p.8] is 0.40 V, leaving >= 11.6 V against 5.2 V needed [ds p.7]. The REF5050's VIN capacitors sit on REF_VIN, after this resistor, so R and C filter ahead of the clamp. Same part as R-LED-SER (UNI-ROYAL 0805W8F3300T5E).

description: 15 V zener clamp on the REF5050 input (MMSZ5245BT1G)
notes: Cathode to REF_VIN, anode to AGND_INST. Vz 14.25-15.75 V at 8.5 mA, Zzt 16 ohm max [ds ONSEMI-MMSZ5221BT1-SERIES-MMSZ5245BT1G.pdf p.3]: at 26 mA it holds <= 16.1 V, under the REF5050's 18 V [calc]. Leakage is specified only at 11 V (0.1 uA); 1 uA through R-REF-IN would be 0.33 mV, so it cannot move the reference [calc].

description: Anti-alias cap at the MCP3202 input pin
notes: 564Hz with the divider's 6k Thevenin (10k||15k) - matches the 500Hz channel everywhere else. WAS 220nF, which is 121Hz and smears the breath band; the '~600Hz, 58dB at 496kHz' note was wrong twice over - wrong corner, and the R-78E5.0 switches at 330kHz not 496kHz. 55dB at 330kHz. C0G not X7R in a DC-accurate path

description: Bulk at MCP3202 VDD/VREF
notes: FITTED, beside C-DEC-ADC at U-ADC pin 8 (VDD, which IS the reference: the MCP3202 has no VREF pin), returned to AGND_INST. The reservoir each conversion draws from, taking the ribbon's inductance out of that current's path. IT DOES NOT FILTER LED PWM: against the ribbon conductor and the LDO it corners in the hundreds of kHz (breath-adc.md). Whether PWM ripple on the reference reaches the breath reading is E9's scope test, specified on breath-adc.md. Samsung CL31B106KBHNNNE (LCSC C89632), 10 uF X7R 50 V, the same part as C-REF-OUT

description: Lower leg of the 0.6x divider from the breath buffer to the ADC
notes: LOWER LEG, to the instrument analog star. 15k against the 10k upper leg is the 0.6x that lands sensor-full-scale inside a 3V3 ADC's range. The RATIO is what matters, so buy both legs from one reel

description: Upper leg of the 0.6x divider from the breath buffer to the ADC
notes: UPPER LEG, AND >=10k IS THE SPEC, NOT THE VALUE: below that, 5V-before-3V3 sequencing pushes about 2.5 mA into the ADC's ESD clamp on every power-up. It also has to leave C-AA-ADC time to settle, which is what stops the leg going higher still. Divide AFTER the buffer, never before

description: 12-bit 2-ch SAR ADC SPI
notes: SOIC-8. VDD-referenced so no separate ref chip. 50ksps at 3V3 vs 4-8kHz needed. One spare channel | 2026-09-21, from Microchip DS21034F now at datasheets/analog/MCP3202-CI-SN.pdf: fCLK max is 1.8MHz at VDD=5V and 0.9MHz at VDD=2.7V, WITH NO 3.3V ROW. The 0.9MHz the design uses is therefore the GUARANTEED 2.7V MAXIMUM, not an interpolation - two documents called it an interpolation and it is strictly conservative at 3.3V, with ~25% of unclaimed headroom (straight-line to 3.3V gives ~1.14MHz). Both rows are characterised, not 100% tested. ALSO A MINIMUM NOBODY HAD: the sample cap holds charge for at least 1.2ms at 85C, so effective fCLK >= ~10kHz - which forecloses 'slow the ADC down' as a way to buy loop time. Sample cap 20pF with 1k switch resistance; tSAMPLE is 1.5 clock cycles and source impedance adds directly to it, so the buffer ahead of it is load-bearing

description: Quad buffer as LED data level shifter
notes: SOIC-14. 5V rail TTL thresholds so 3.3V reads high. ONE GATE USED, THREE SPARE: the LED row has one data line (ADR 0028); tie every spare input. LED 1's DIN2 is grounded, not driven. THRESHOLD: the WS2815B-V1 wants V_IH 2.7V min and V_IL 1.5V max at VDD 12V, and takes -0.3 to 5.7V on a logic input [ds datasheets/led/WS2815B-V1.pdf pp.2-3]; this part's output at 5V clears the first and stays under the last (led-strip-drive.md section 4)

description: HF decoupling at every carrier IC - ADC, reference, buffer, level shifter, sensor
notes: One per supply pin, six: C-DEC-ADC (MCP3202), C-DEC-REF-VIN and C-DEC-REF-VOUT (REF5050 IN and OUT), C-DEC-BUF (OPA2197 +12V), C-DECOUPLE-LED (74AHCT125) and C-DEC-SENSOR (U-BREATH VS, pin 2). The REF5050 wants both: a VIN bypass and a high-frequency capacitor between the output and ground [ds SBOS410O section 9.4.1.1 pp.29-30]. C-DEC-SENSOR is the 100nF the reference buffer's compensation is designed against - see figures.yaml cref-out-node. The shift registers have their own, C-DECOUPLE-165

description: Series resistor on the LED row's data line at the driver
notes: Damps the fastest edge in the instrument at its source and protects the 74AHCT125 output. ONE: the row has one data line, and it feeds LED 1's DIN1 and LED 2's DIN2 (ADR 0028). LED 1's DIN2 is grounded, so it needs no gate and no resistor

description: Pull-down on the LED data line at the MCU pin
notes: IO1 is high-impedance through the bootloader window, and a floating data line into addressable LEDs is the classic source of intermittent LED behaviour. FITTED: the ESP32-S3 datasheet gives GPIO1 no weak pull at or after reset (p.16), so the line floats in the boot window on every board. 10k holds the AHCT input at 10mV against its 1uA leakage (V_IL 0.8V) - led-strip-drive.md. One part, one data line (ADR 0028)

part: WS2815B-V1, 12V addressable RGB LED, 5050 PLCC6, with a backup data input
description: The instrument's lights: one row down the main board's top-face centreline, lighting both acrylic sides through the cavity
notes: COUNT: config/body.yaml lighting.led_count; pitch and positions from the body CAD (pcb-geometry.echo 'led'). ONE DATA LINE, BACKUP CHAINED: DIN1 from the LED before's DO, DIN2 from the LED before's DIN1, LED 1's DIN2 to GND - the WS2815 recommended circuit [ds datasheets/led/WS2815.pdf p.4]; the B-V1 sheet draws none. PIN 1 IS NC and the body's chamfer marks PIN 1, bottom right in the numbered pin drawing [ds datasheets/led/WS2815B-V1.pdf p.2]: check the assembler's rotation against the footprint. 12V on VDD, 9.5-13.5V absolute [ds p.2]. MSL 5a: baked before reflow [ds p.6]; no repair after reflow in a glued body. JLC EXTENDED part, LCSC C5446699. Current: tracked figure led-row-current

description: Bypass at each D-LED, VDD (pin 2) to GND (pin 5)
notes: ONE PER D-LED, at its VDD pin. The vendor's 100 nF bypass [ds datasheets/led/WS2815.pdf p.4, 'C1 is bypass filter capacitor']. The same part as C-DECOUPLE-CARRIER, 50V on the 12V row

description: Service header: the real-time board's U0TXD, U0RXD, GND, EN and IO0
notes: FIVE PINS (ADR 0018): 1 TXD (IO43, out), 2 RXD (IO44, in), 3 GND, 4 EN, 5 IO0 - the ground between the UART pair and the control pair. EN and IO0 reach it on two conductors of CBL-MCU-RIBBON, soldered on the Matrix to its Key1 (RESET/EN) and Key2 (BOOT/IO0) terminals. NOTHING IN SERIES: the Matrix pulls both up with 10k to its 3V3 (R8, R10) and its buttons pull them to GND [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf]. DRIVE THEM TO GROUND ONLY - a button, a jumper, or an adapter's open-collector reset circuit; never drive them high, least of all from a 5V adapter. Recovery order: USB-Serial-JTAG through the tail USB-C first, a reflash over the same port second, this header third - and with EN and IO0 here, download mode can be forced in place (firmware/README.md)

description: Real-time MCU: ESP32-S3 + onboard QMI8658C 6-axis IMU
package: dev board, on the lid; CBL-MCU-RIBBON soldered to its pad rows
notes: Mounted low for acceleration sensitivity. 17 GPIO on its two pad rows (1-7, 33-40, 43, 44) and 12 used; CBL-MCU-RIBBON takes them to J-MCU. Native USB - verified, not a UART bridge - so USB MIDI works. 4MB flash, 2MB QUAD PSRAM, both on-package: the vendor schematic marks U66 = ESP32-S3FH4R2 [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf; F=in-package flash, H4=4MB, R2=2MB quad PSRAM from Espressif's ordering code, from memory], so GPIO33-37 are free - octal PSRAM would have taken them. The 8x8 matrix is the instrument's only display, under a window in the top face (ADR 0015) - measure idle draw at E1 to size the shared lighting budget

description: Conformal coating for the in-body boards
notes: Breathed into for hours behind 18 unsealed switch cutouts, interior 10-20K above ambient. MASK BOTH SENSOR PORTS FIRST - a sealed reference chamber gains ~5.2kPa when warm and the output clips at zero, looking like a dead sensor (ADR 0003). THE SENSOR IS SOLDERED TO THE BOARD AND COATED WITH IT: a sensor swap breaks the coating at its eight joints - re-mask both ports before touching it up

part: 4-layer PCB - the main board: thumb switches, both thumb registers and the carrier circuits
description: Thumb switches and their registers, breath sensor, reference, ADC, umbilical, SPI egress, LED drive and the LED row, the regulator, service header

notes: CONDUCTORS: 24, conductor n = J-MCU pin n (J-MCU row; hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml is authoritative). AT THE MATRIX END [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf; pad rows per WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-pinout.png]: the 12 used GPIO and the spare IO2 and IO3 to their pads; 3V3 (13) to the 3V3 pad; 5V x3 - conductors 1 and 3 both on the 5V pad, 17 on TP2 (net VCC_5V); GND x4 - conductor 2 on the GND pad, 9, 11 and 15 on TP3 (net GND). IF TP3 WILL NOT TAKE THREE JOINTS, twist 9, 11 and 15 together and tin them as one joint - each is still its own path to J-MCU. EN (24) to Key1 and IO0 (23) to Key2, each on the terminal that goes to its 10k pull-up (R8 for RESET/EN, R10 for IO0), NOT the one on GND: with a meter, the right terminal reads ~10k to the 3V3 pad and the wrong one 0 ohm to the GND pad. Nothing in series on either: R8/R10 hold them up, the buttons still work, and whatever drives them from HDR-SERVICE pulls to ground only. CURRENT: at U-BUCK's 1A (R-78E5.0-1.0) the three 5V conductors carry ~0.33A each and the four GND ~0.25A [calc, equal sharing]; a 0.635mm conductor carries that without heating to speak of [from memory]. RESISTANCE IS WHAT THE FOUR GROUNDS ARE FOR: ~34mohm per 100mm [from memory, ~30AWG], four in parallel ~8.5mohm - ~1 LSB full scale on the breath ADC per 100mA and ~10 at 1A, against ~42 on one ground [calc, carrier.md]. The Matrix's 3V3 is the ADC's reference (carrier/breath-adc) and is regulated against the Matrix's ground, so LED return current in the ribbon's grounds moves it. E11 confirms it: breath output clean while the matrix is exercised. BUILD: split the ribbon at the Matrix end into its pad-row groups; separate each conductor only as far as it travels to its pad, solder, then fix the ribbon to the board so it flexes behind the joints rather than at them [from memory]. Crimp the IDC socket with pin 1 marked. LENGTH: mechanical/drc.echo 'Matrix ribbon length' plus build slack - enough to lift the lid far enough to reach J-MCU. A DEAD MATRIX: unplug at J-MCU, lid off, desolder the ribbon from the pads and solder it (or a new one) to the replacement - a bench job, with no main-board rework

description: 8-bit parallel-in shift register
notes: 74HCS165: SCHMITT-TRIGGER INPUTS, NOT A PLAIN 74HC165. Every key input crosses its thresholds at the key network's RC rate, far slower than a plain HC165 allows; the HCS165 has no input transition-rate requirement (datasheets/logic/SN74HCS165-ti-scls828a.pdf p.15) and the same pinout and SOIC-16 (p.3). Thresholds at 3.3 V: TI publishes rows at 2, 4.5 and 6 V only, so key-release-time and key-press-time are taken at its extreme ratios (their threshold_note). HC-FAMILY OUTPUTS, NOT LVC: over an unterminated line stronger drive and faster edges are what ring, and HC drive is the weaker. A hop is NOT a lumped load (output transition is published as a maximum only, p.8, and a hop is longer than key-chain-loom.md's length rule allows even at that maximum); it does not need to be: QH to the next SER is data sampled a whole clock period later, into a Schmitt input (setup and hold, p.7), and the edge-sensitive SCK and SH/LD are the MCU's, behind R-CHAIN-SER (E14). LVC with source termination is the way back if E4 or E14 disagrees. ONE PER CLUSTER: right_thumb and left_thumb on the main board, right_hand and left_hand on the key boards (ADR 0017). Tie CLK INH low at all four. A board house substitute must have Schmitt-trigger inputs with no transition-rate limit: a 74HC165 or a 74LV165A (whose Schmitt action still carries a rate limit, datasheets/logic/74LV165A-nexperia.pdf p.5) is not one. The bought part is the sheet's (ADR 0019)

description: Pull-up on every 74x165 key input
notes: 2k2, on the register input's node, placed beside its switch. Kept as cheap insurance: the cavity is breathed into for hours at 10-20K above ambient and the switch contacts are open. Its cost is the per-pressed-key draw (key-scan-current) on the rail that is also the ADC reference - a live trade, key-switch-network.md. TWENTY-FOUR: one per switch position including the reserved spare-switch bits (config/key-layout.yaml spare_bits_switches), PLUS one on each genuinely free bit (free-bits): a floating free bit is the ADR 0001 fix-6 fault, and unretrofittable. A free bit's pull-up draws only the input's leakage, since nothing pulls that node low. Why 2k2 and not 10k: notes.md

description: Series resistor between each switch and its 74x165 input
notes: With C-KEY: press crosses the register's lower threshold (VT-, at its minimum) at key-press-time so it stays instant, and release crosses its upper threshold (VT+, at its maximum) at key-release-time. Both are tracked figures and are not restated here - the network they are computed on is 2k2/47nF. The RC is a GLITCH filter, not the debounce: the switch's bounce (ks33-contact-bounce) is far longer, and firmware's release window rejects it. THIS RESISTOR'S JOB: it sets the pressed-node divider and LIMITS C-KEY'S DISCHARGE INTO THE SWITCH CONTACT on every press. It is not in front of the register input and protects nothing there. The press transient against the KS-33's contact rating, and the open trade to a larger value and the ceiling VT- min puts on it: key-switch-network.md

description: Filter cap at each 74x165 key input
notes: 47nF with the 2k2 pull-up keeps tau at ~103us. Press crosses the register's lower threshold (VT-, at its minimum) at key-press-time - see that figure for the margin against the 250us scan period - and release crosses its upper threshold (VT+, at its maximum) at key-release-time. The thresholds are those figures' threshold_note, not restated here. *** DO NOT JUSTIFY THIS PART BY THE COUPLING ARGUMENT: IT IS WRONG (see ADR 0001). *** A capacitive divider cannot exceed the aggressor's swing, and on the real 5V data line an unfiltered wire sees 1.36V of swing, landing the idle node at 1.94V - above the register's VT- even at its maximum, which is at most 0.5 x VCC in every row TI publishes, 1.65V at 3.3V [calc; datasheets/logic/SN74HCS165-ti-scls828a.pdf p.6]: about 0.3V clear, so an unfiltered wire would not read as a press, but not by much. The filter is cheap insurance and a GLITCH filter, not the debounce (key-switch-network.md); it is not the thing that makes the topology safe

notes: TWO, not one, and 1206 not 0805 - both changed with the schematic and this row did not follow. description: ESD protection on the BREATH and AGND legs

Worse, ADR 0003's buffer-on-+12V decision exists precisely so a SUSTAINED +12V fault on BREATH is harmless - a 5V clamp turns that designed-safe case into a part that conducts until something fails. PESD12VS1UA,115 (LCSC C131084), SOD-323: VRWM 12 V, VBR 13.3 V min [ds NEXPERIA-PESD12VS1UA.pdf p.5], so a sustained +12 V does not conduct; leakage 100 nA max at 12 V, 0.1 mV across the 1k [calc]. NOT THE UB: PESD12VS1UB is SOD523 [ds NEXPERIA-PESD12VS1UB.pdf p.1], 0402-class. The UA's 180 pF max behind the 1k is a pole at 0.88 MHz, far above the breath band [calc]

description: SPI idle-state pulls at the module: SCLK and MOSI (cable side), SCLK_DAC, DIN and SYNC (DAC side)
notes: FIVE OF THE MODULE'S SIX SPI PULLS - the sixth, CS_MOD's cable-side pull, is its own row, R-CS-PULL-MOD, because it is 100k and not 10k, and it has a partner at the instrument end, R-CS-PULL-INST (spi-link.md, 'CS_MOD's two pulls'). BOTH SIDES of the 74AHCT125. Cable side: SCLK and MOSI to DIG_GND, so the buffer's inputs do not float and crowbar when the instrument is absent. DAC side: SCLK_DAC and DIN down, SYNC up. They were bought for a buffer whose OE could be disabled; its OE is now tied on and its VCC is the DAC's own rail, so they matter only if the buffer fails with its outputs open. Kept as insurance on the one failure that latches (spi-link.md, 'Pulls on both sides of the buffer'). Module-alive-instrument-off is the normal state, not a fault; a stray CS edge latches garbage into the pitch DAC. DAC-SIDE SYNC PULLS TO AVDD (U-REG-DAC's rail, dac-rail), a pull-up on its consumer's rail: on any other rail a reversed ribbon could reach the DAC's SYNC pin and turn a $0.30 buffer failure into a DAC failure. UNI-ROYAL 0805W8F1002T5E, LCSC C17414

description: CS_MOD's cable-side pull-up at the module, to LOGIC_5V
notes: THE WEAK HALF OF CS_MOD'S TWO PULLS (the strong half is R-CS-PULL-INST at the instrument). On module-main as R-PULL-CS, from CS_MOD to LOGIC_5V - the rail of the part it holds, U-RX-MOD, whose first Schmitt gate it reaches through R-RX-CS (the 74AHCT125 behind it is on DAC_AVDD). 100k, NOT 10k: with the instrument plugged in and switched off, its 3V3 is dead, and 10k to 5V would push ~430uA through the ESP32's input clamp with the node stuck near 0.7V; 100k against R-CS-PULL-INST's 10k puts ~45uA into the dead rail and the node at ~0.45V, 50mV under U-RX-MOD's lowest V_T- of 0.5V [ds SN74AHCT14.pdf p.5] - so SYNC may read either way in that state, and either is harmless (spi-link.md, 'CS_MOD's two pulls'). With nothing plugged in it holds the receiver's input within 0.1V of 5V (1uA max input current [ds SN74AHCT14.pdf p.5]), so SYNC sits high and the DAC ignores SCLK. A PULL-DOWN HERE IS WRONG: the receive path does not invert (U-RX-MOD inverts twice), so it would hold SYNC low - selected - with the umbilical out. FB must be divided down from the output at all - see U-LOADSW for why an open FB latches the part off. *** V_FB = 0.5V AND THE PWRGD THRESHOLD V_FBH = 1.313V ARE SET BY THE SAME DIVIDER, *** so V_OUT(full 47mV limit) = 0.381 x V_OUT(PWRGD) ALWAYS - 'cross 0.5V early in the ramp' and 'PWRGD means the output is good' are ONE decision, not two, and the ratio is fixed by the part, not by these resistors. It is therefore sized at the PWRGD end, which is the end with a hard requirement: PWRGD must release below the worst-case delivered output of ~11.36V (Eurorack +12V at -5%, less the sense and FET drops). The foldback law behind it, verbatim [p.5, drawn as Figure 7 p.9]: 'The current limit circuit will regulate the voltage across the sense resistor (VCC - VSENSE) to 47mV when VFB is 0.5V or higher. If VFB drops below 0.5V, the voltage across the sense resistor decreases linearly and stops at 12mV when VFB is 0V.' Divider current is 294uA at 12V, 294x the 1uA max FB input current [p.2], so leakage is <=0.34% of the ratio

notes: NORMALLY OPEN, AND IT IS COPPER - NOTHING IS ORDERED FOR THIS ROW, but the layout must carry the footprint. description: Straps the DAC8568 LDAC pin to GND
notes: *** LDAC MUST BE STRAPPED TO GND, NOT PULLED TO AVDD - PULLING IT HIGH GATES THE DAC. *** SBAS430E p.38, verbatim: 'For such synchronous updates, the LDAC pin is not required and it must be connected to GND permanently.' Same page: the internal LDAC register defaults to 0x00, and 'if the LDAC register bit is set to 0, the DAC channel is controlled by the LDAC pin'. So register at default plus pin high means the buffer-to-DAC-register transfer is BLOCKED - and with no MISO, firmware can never discover it. A module that accepts every word and moves no output. A hardware LDAC was considered and declined, so the six populated channels update as each word lands. WORTH REVISITING AT FIRMWARE TIME: SBAS430E Table 11 p.36 offers 'Write to DAC input register Ch X and update all DAC registers (SW LDAC)', so five plain writes then one update-all as the last word of each pass gives a SIMULTANEOUS update inside the six words already budgeted - taking the 100-200us CLR-exit window to zero for no parts and no ninth conductor

description: Octal 16-bit DAC SPI, internal reference
notes: *** THE ORDER CODE IS DAC8568ICPW(R), NOT DAC8568CIPW. *** Buy ICPWR, the reel of the same part: LCSC stocks it where it barely stocks ICPW [web 2026-09-29]. DAC8568CIPW appears ZERO times in SBAS430E; the Package Option Addendum [pp.54-57] enumerates DAC8568IAPW / IBPW / ICPW / IDPW and the R reel variants. The I and the grade letter are transposed in several places including the banked file's own NAME, datasheets/analog/DAC8568CIPW.pdf - the file and its SHA are correct and renaming it would mean editing another wave's manifest fragment, which CLAUDE.md 4 forbids, so the fact is recorded here per repo-maintenance.md 3. GRADE LOCKED TO C, and the letter selects REFERENCE GAIN as well as reset state: A/B are gain 1 (2.500V full scale), C/D gain 2 (5.000V). An A-grade part would halve everything - pitch -2 to +2.25V, mods +/-5V - and channel 7 could not reach 2.500V at all. C also clears to ZERO scale where B/D clear to midscale and would park pitch octaves up: 'For device grades A and C on power-up, all DAC registers are filled with zeros and the output voltages of all DAC channels are set to zero scale.' *** THE C GRADE REQUIRES AVDD 5.0V TO 5.5V *** - C/D are specified only over that range where A/B are 2.7-5.5V. U-REG-DAC (LT3042, set by R-SET-DAC) holds dac-rail inside it on every part with nothing to adjust (power-entry.md, 'The DAC rail'); 5.00V IS STILL A HARD FLOOR - never substitute R-SET-DAC. External VREFIN must be <= AVDD/2 on C/D against <= AVDD on A/B - not binding while the internal reference is used, but it forecloses an external-reference retrofit above ~2.6V. Reference tempco is GRADE-DEPENDENT: C/D 2 typ / 5 max ppm/degC against A/B 5 typ / 25 max, so the 5 ppm/degC in the pitch error budget is the C-grade MAX and is the right number. Populate 6 of 8: pitch, 4 mods, mod offset; channels 6 and 8 spare. Static reference mode auto-powers the reference with the DACs and Flexible mode (DB19=1) keeps it up regardless, but BOTH default to reference OFF after any power cycle - enable at boot

description: DAC8568 reference output filter, VREFIN/VREFOUT to AGND_MOD
notes: THE DATASHEET'S OWN: 'A minimum 100nF capacitor is recommended between the reference output and GND for noise filtering' [SBAS430E p.31]. At the pin. VREFOUT is also the pitch stage's reference, so this is the only filter on the node the whole 1 V/oct tracking argument rests on. While the reference is disabled the pin is 3-state and TRIM-OFFSET's 10k discharges this cap to 0 V in about 1 ms. CC0805KRX7R9BB104, LCSC C49678

description: Level shifter, 3V3 SPI up to 5V for the DAC
notes: SAME part as the instrument LED shifter. Covers SCLK MOSI CS with a spare gate, each from U-RX-MOD's second inverter. *** VCC IS DAC_AVDD, THE DAC'S OWN RAIL (U-REG-DAC), NOT LOGIC_5V. *** Its outputs are the DAC8568's SYNC, SCLK and DIN, whose absolute maximum is AVDD + 0.3V [ds DAC8568CIPW.pdf p.2]; LOGIC_5V arrives first and leaves last, so on it these pins would sit volts over AVDD for milliseconds at every power-up and power-down - do not move it back (digital-and-supervision/sim, rails-and-sync and its what-if). Its inputs come from U-RX-MOD on LOGIC_5V and sit above its VCC while DAC_AVDD is low, which the no-clamp property below makes legal. *** NO INPUT CLAMP TO VCC, *** confirmed three independent ways in SCLS264O: abs-max lists 'Input clamp current, IIK (VI < 0): -20mA', NEGATIVE ONLY, against an output clamp specified BOTH ways; abs-max input voltage is -0.5 to 7V stated WITHOUT reference to VCC where the output is -0.5 to VCC+0.5; and input leakage is specified as +/-1uA max AT VI = 5.5V WITH VCC = 0V, which TI could not guarantee if a VCC clamp existed. THAT IS WHAT MAKES BACK-DRIVING AN UNPOWERED MODULE SAFE. Its inputs are driven by U-RX-MOD, the Schmitt stage, not by the cable: the thresholds the link is analysed against are U-RX-MOD's. Drive +/-8mA; input transition rate must be <= 20ns/V; TIE EVERY UNUSED INPUT TO VCC OR GND. *** OE IS TIED ENABLED AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. *** The presence-gated OE is deleted along with its comparator: the threshold sat inside the breath signal's own range, it locked out every standalone-module milestone, and it failed toward 'present'. What it was protecting against - floating CMOS at the DAC while the instrument is off - is what the five R-SPI-PULL and R-PULL-CS are for, and running the buffer unconditionally is what every surveyed Eurorack module does

description: SPI receiver: hex Schmitt-trigger inverter, SCLK MOSI CS each through two gates, ahead of U-LVL-MOD
notes: THE SPI LINK'S RECEIVER (owner, 2026-09-30: 'add buffer' - with hysteresis, at the receiving end). The cable's SCLK/MOSI pair couples each SCLK edge into MOSI for about one round trip, far enough to cross a plain TTL input's thresholds (spi-pair-crosstalk); behind R-RX-MOD and C-RX-MOD this input does not see it (interfaces/spi-link/sim). TTL-COMPATIBLE: VT+ 0.9-2.1V, VT- 0.5-1.7V over VCC 4.5-5.5V, HYSTERESIS 0.4V MIN [ds SN74AHCT14.pdf p.5]. INVERTING: each signal uses two gates, so all six are used and none needs a tie. *** NO INPUT CLAMP TO VCC, *** like U-LVL-MOD: I_IK is specified for VI < 0 only [p.4] and I_I is +/-1uA at VCC = 0V [p.5], so a powered instrument back-driving an unpowered module is still safe - do not substitute a 74HCT14, whose inputs clamp to VCC. From LOGIC_5V, decoupled by C-DEC-RX (a C-DECOUPLE). tpd 1-9ns [p.6]. TI SN74AHCT14DR, LCSC C141316

description: Series half of the RC ahead of each U-RX-MOD input
notes: THREE: R-RX-SCLK, R-RX-MOSI, R-RX-CS, from the cable node (where the R-SPI-PULL and R-CS-PULL-MOD pulls stay) to U-RX-MOD's first gate. With C-RX-MOD, 47ns: the cable's crosstalk and reflections last about one round trip and reach the Schmitt input far inside its hysteresis (interfaces/spi-link/sim). 1k against the line's 50-280 ohm modes is near-open, so it leaves the line's termination as it was. The 10k pull-downs are at the cable node, ahead of this resistor, and the gate input draws no current, so the settled high at the input is the cable node's: 3.3 x 10k / (10k + 82R R-SPI-SER + ~35R of pad) = ~3.26V, above VT+ max 2.1V [calc]. UNI-ROYAL 0805W8F1001T5E, LCSC C17513

description: Shunt half of the RC ahead of each U-RX-MOD input
notes: THREE: C-RX-SCLK, C-RX-MOSI, C-RX-CS, U-RX-MOD's input pin to DIG_GND, at the pin. C0G so the time constant does not move with bias or temperature; +/-5% is in the sim's corners. description: Dual low-drift RRIO op-amp
notes: ONE op-amp part throughout the module, and THIS ROW IS WHERE THE OPA2197'S DEVICE FACTS LIVE - U-BUF and U-RESP cite it rather than repeat it. Six packages, twelve halves, TEN used: pitch, mod 1-4, mod offset follower, VREFOUT follower, breath REF-zero buffer, breath gain buffer, breath summer. TWO SPARE (U-REF-BUF B, U-MOD-C B); the response shaper is its own package, U-RESP, and takes neither. RRIO on +/-12V reaches ~11.9V. FROM THE BANKED SBOS737C: open-loop output impedance is SPECIFIED at 375 ohm [EC table p.8 and p.10, f = 1 MHz], with Figure 26 giving ~3.26k at 0.1Hz, 482 at 10Hz, a 375 plateau from 100Hz to 300kHz, 301 at 1MHz and ~73 at 10MHz - *** DO NOT SIZE A POLE OFF THE 10MHz VALUE, *** which is roughly 5x optimistic. Capacitive load is 1 nF max [p.1 Features, 7.3.5 p.22: 'in a unity-gain configuration, directly drives up to 1 nF of pure capacitive load'], and Figures 27/28 show that is a stable-but-RINGING limit, ~40% overshoot at unity gain - TI recommends a 10-20 ohm isolation resistor and tabulates R_ISO for 45/60 deg phase margin in Table 3 p.23. GBW 10MHz, SR 20V/us, Isc +/-65mA, IQ 1mA/amp, ~11.9V swing on +/-12V, SOIC-8 DUAL R-thJA 107.9 degC/W - note the SINGLE OPA197 is 115.8 and is a different table. PSRR is +/-1 uV/V typ and +/-3 uV/V max, i.e. 120 dB typ and 110.5 dB worst case; the '114 dB' figure is not in the document

part: 10k multiturn cermet + divider from the DAC rail (dac-rail)
description: Nulls the sensor's +0.265V pedestal at the INA828 REF pin
notes: Buffered by a half of U-OPA-PITCH - REF needs a low source impedance or it degrades CMRR one-for-one. *** RANGE 0 TO +1.0V, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE PEDESTAL IS A SPEC BAND, NOT A TYPICAL *** - the datasheet's own table gives Voff 0.152 / 0.265 / 0.378 V, so the REF needed spans 0.328-0.817V at the effective gain 2.16106. A 0.6V ceiling would leave a part at the top of its own spec UN-NULLABLE, with 1.4-5.6% of span standing at the jack; +1.0V covers the whole band with margin. The setting itself is the tracked figure breath-zero-ref; do not restate it. *** DERIVE IT FROM THE DAC RAIL (dac-rail), NOT FROM VREFOUT. *** VREFOUT is the DAC's internal reference and is DISABLED at power-on until firmware writes an enable, so taking the breath zero from it would make the analog breath path depend on a DAC register - which three documents correctly say it does not. The DAC rail is up whenever +12V is. THIS IS ALSO WHAT MAKES THE PANEL KNOBS INDEPENDENT: with REF grounded the pedestal sits upstream of the gain pot and gets multiplied. One zero authority per representation still holds - this is CALIBRATION, set once, where the panel OFFSET knob is PERFORMANCE

description: Instrumentation amp - breath receiver, senses against AGND
notes: BREATH drives IN-, AGND drives IN+, and REF is driven by TRIM-BREATH-ZERO THROUGH A BUFFER - never a bare divider, because source impedance on an in-amp REF pin degrades CMRR one-for-one. *** THE NUMBER IS 5 OHMS *** [SBOS792A section 8.1, verbatim: 'For the best performance, keep the source impedance to the REF terminal, RREF, below 5 ohm'] - RREF sits in series with one of the internal 40k difference-amp resistors and unbalances the bridge. Output runs 0V at rest to inamp-full-scale: Vout = -2.16106*(V_BREATH - V_AGND) + V_REF, with TRIM-BREATH-ZERO nulling the sensor pedestal. *** NOTE THE GAIN: 2.16106 IS THE EFFECTIVE GAIN, *** the raw G = 1 + 50k/42.2k = 2.185 times the 1M/(1M+11k) bias divider - using the raw 2.185 is the recorded way to get this wrong. The DAC ch6 zero injection that originally justified the input swap is deleted (ADR 0003). EMI: the part HAS an integrated RFI filter, -3dB at 53MHz, and EMIRR is a TABULATED characteristic rather than just a curve. *** THE WORST CASES ARE 48dB DIFFERENTIAL AT 400MHz AND 51dB COMMON-MODE AT 1.8GHz, *** and the differential and common-mode columns INVERT between 900MHz (52/98) and 1.8GHz (94/51) - so any RF-rectification argument must use those two and not the 90-plus dB numbers. TI does not claim the internal filter is sufficient on its own. See breath-receive-stage.md

description: Compensation cap, op-amp OUTPUT to the inverting input
notes: FROM THE OP-AMP OUTPUT TO THE (-) INPUT. NOT 'across the feedback resistor' - with the tap at the jack, R2 spans jack-to-(-), so a cap across R2 connects the same two nodes and leaves R-OUT-PROT inside the loop at every frequency: 18 degrees of phase margin with 2m of cable, under 10 with four destinations. Three documents said 'across R2' and were wrong. 2.2nF with C-FILT-PITCH restored is maximally flat, -3dB at 12.2kHz. IT IS NOT A FILTER: a cap in the feedback of a NON-INVERTING stage gives (2+sRC)/(1+sRC), a pole and a zero an octave up, flattening at unity - 6.02dB maximum for any value. Two independent reviews found this separately

description: Anti-alias/glitch filter on the pitch DAC input, ahead of the op-amp
notes: THE ACTUAL PITCH FILTER. 15.9kHz against R-OPAMP-IN's 1k, on a node with NO LOOP AROUND IT. C-FB-PITCH cannot do this job: a cap across the feedback resistor of a NON-INVERTING stage gives (2+sRC)/(1+sRC) - a pole at 7.2kHz (R2 + TRIM-GAIN against 2.2nF) and a zero an octave above, flattening at unity, so 6.02dB of attenuation maximum for any value. It is a shelf, not a pole. Filtering the DAC before the stage is also what the surveyed designs do

description: Reconstruction and RF shunt at the pitch jack
notes: RESTORED. It was deleted on the reasoning that a cap on the feedback node sits inside the DC loop at the handover; two independent loop analyses then put 10nF there and found phase margin UNCHANGED, because C-FB-PITCH ties the (-) input to the op-amp OUTPUT so beta(inf)=1 and R-OUT-PROT isolates the jack above the handover. The feedback network is a LEAD at every load tried - open, 200pF, 800pF, 10nF, dead short. Deleting it cost 30dB at 1MHz and left the connector with no low-impedance shunt at all

The identical problem was already found and fixed on the breath in-amp (R-BIAS-INAMP); this is the same fix on the six DAC-driven nodes

description: Matched resistor network for pitch scaling
package: MSOP-8 MS8E (0.65mm pitch) WITH 1.88 x 1.68mm EXPOSED PAD
notes: RATIO IS 1:1 - the pitch stage is a non-inverting amp with the reference at the bottom of the feedback divider (see pitch-stage.md). Two of four sections used. ORDER CODE IS TWO LETTER FIELDS: LT5400 + <A|B matching> + <C|I|H|MP temp> + MS8E-1#PBF. The -1 option is the four-equal-10k 1:1 quad and THERE IS NO 1:3 OPTION [p.2 table: -1 10k 1:1, -2 100k 1:1, -3 1:10, -4 1k 1:1, -5 1M 1:1, -6 1:5]. Grade A is 0.01% matching, B 0.025%; A degrades to +/-0.0125% over -40/+85degC while B is flat. MUST BE THE MS8 (MSOP) OPTION, NOT THE LEADLESS DFN. *** MS8E HAS AN EXPOSED PAD *** [p.2, p.8] - the footprint is MSOP-8-1EP_3x3mm_P0.65mm_EP1.68x1.88mm, NOT a plain MSOP-8. WHERE THE PAD GOES [p.6]: not DC-connected to any resistor, 'do not tie the exposed pad to noisy signals or noisy grounds', 'connecting the exposed pad to a quiet AC ground is recommended'. THE PAD GOES TO AGND_MOD (pitch-stage.md, 'The LT5400's exposed pad'): pad-to-resistor coupling is 5.5 pF against 1.4 pF resistor-to-resistor, so the pad is the dominant stray on the 1V/oct node. The sheet's symbol carries it as pin 9, EP. The two spare sections are tied to AGND_MOD at both ends. Ratio tracking 1 ppm/degC MAX (0.2 typ). ABSOLUTE tolerance is +/-7.5% (A) / +/-15% (B), which sets TRIM-GAIN's real authority, +/-100/(R + 100) about R-GAIN-CTR, at +/-0.86% to +/-1.16% on the B part rather than a nominal +/-1% - still several times the DAC's +/-0.15% FSR gain error (SBAS430E p.3). WHY THE PART IS KEPT, since its own tempco is currently masked: the DAC's internal reference drifts 0.42 cents over 10degC and cannot be trimmed, against 0.027 for the LT5400 and 0.38 for two 0.1%/10ppm discretes - $8 permanently solves the one term that can be, on a board built once, and attacking the reference later is only worth doing if the network is already there. CAVEAT FOR ANYONE EDITING ADR 0006: the banked rev fa's option table ends at -6, so LT5400-7 and 'a 1:4 offered directly' are NOT-IN-DOCUMENT rather than refuted - do not 'correct' ADR 0006 by citing rev fa's silence. 5400fc.pdf is still wanted. ORDERED AS LT5400BIMS8E-1#PBF [p.3 order table]: B GRADE because the static ratio error is trimmed out by TRIM-GAIN and B's 0.025% is flat over temperature where A's 0.01% degrades to 0.0125% - the drift, not the initial match, is what is left after trim, and it is the same 0.2 ppm/C for both; I GRADE (-40 to +85 C) for the rack in a van, as U-LOADSW. notes: Partner of R-VREF-FB. Thin film, 25 ppm/C. RT0805BRD0710KL, LCSC C110775

description: Jack-side ESD clamp on the pitch jack tip, ahead of the LT5400
notes: BIDIRECTIONAL, TIP TO SLEEVE, AT THE PITCH JACK ON THE MODULE JACK BOARD - not on module-main, so a strike is clamped before it crosses J-B2B-MOD. WHY: the jack tip reaches RN-PITCH's R2 through TRIM-GAIN's 0-200R and nothing else, and the LT5400 has no internal ESD diodes: +/-1kV HBM, 'ESD beyond this voltage can damage or degrade the device including causing pin-to-pin shorts' [LT5400.pdf p.6]; its Figure 1 offers diodes to the rails or 'bidirectional Zeners to ground' at the connector, and the jack board has no rails. MUST BE BIDIRECTIONAL with standoff above 12V: the jack swings -2.5 to +7.5V and a patch can put another module's +/-12V on it; a unidirectional part would conduct at -0.7V. PESD15VL1BA [NEXPERIA-PESD15VL1BA.pdf p.4]: VRWM 15V; VBR 17.1V min at 5mA; IRM 50nA max at 15V; Cd 16pF typ at 0V; VCL 25V at 1A, 44V at IPPM 5A (8/20us); IEC 61000-4-2 30kV contact [p.3]. 44V is inside the LT5400's 80V across any two pins [LT5400.pdf p.2]. NO ACCURACY COST: it sits on JACK_TIP, which is the DC feedback node, so its leakage is a load inside the loop like any VCO (zero error), and 16pF beside C-FILT-PITCH's 10nF is 0.16 percent of it, inside that part's own tolerance; pitch-stage/sim runs the stage with it fitted. Returns to AGND_MOD at the jack sleeve, not to a rail, so it cannot back-power the module the way a rail clamp at the jack did (D-JACK-CLAMP). ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate.. 82nF C0G 50V EXISTS IN 1206: Murata GRM31C5C1H823JA01L, LCSC C97947 [ds MURATA-GRM31C5C1H823JA01L-82NF-C0G-1206.pdf]

It is the RATIO with R-MODGAIN-FB that has to hold, not either absolute value: SPECIFIED 0.1 % (owner, 2026-10-01), both values from ONE SERIES AND TCR GRADE, Yageo RT0805BRD07 (B = 0.1 %, D = 25 ppm/C [ds datasheets/discrete-and-power/YAGEO-RT-THIN-FILM-CHIP-RESISTOR-RT0805FRE0710KL.pdf p.2]), which holds the ratio to 0.2 % [calc] - two values cannot come off one reel. THE POWER RATING IS NOT OPTIONAL AND THIS IS THE ONLY PART IN THE MODULE AT REAL RISK FROM ANY JACK FAULT. *** The worst case is output-to-output patching, not a short: with pitch taking jack-side feedback the loop FIGHTS the other module, giving 322mW against a 220R source at +/-10V (two reviewers found this independently, on 269/312/464mW ladders). A dead short merely rails the op-amp across this resistor, at 142mW. AND THE DERATING IS WHAT RULES OUT 500mW: thick-film at a 50C rack interior leaves a 500mW 1206 delivering 350-420mW, so it is ~1.1x margin, not the 2.6x a nameplate reading suggests. description: Clamp diodes on the DRIVER side of R-OUT-PROT

(a) BACK-POWERING: clamped at the JACK, a neighbouring module driving 10V through its own 220R output pushes 42mA per jack into our +12V rail when this module is off - 254mA across six jacks, into the rail that also feeds the umbilical. Behind the 1k it is 7.6mA per jack. (b) LEAKAGE: inside the feedback loop the op-amp absorbs it, so the 2.4-cent BAT54S error goes to identically zero for any diode. BAV99 kept anyway - silicon costs nothing and the reasoning no longer depends on it. NOTE: no surveyed design clamps a CV output to the RAILS at all; every clamp in the corpus goes to GND. Erica Synths is the one that puts its clamp on the driver side, which is where this now is. SIX - one per OUTPUT jack including breath, whose schematic omitted it. The two BREATH INPUT clamps are a separate row, D-CLAMP-BREATH, so the module carries eight BAV99 in total

Body 9 x 9 x 8.3mm, barrel bore D3.6, 3.5mm of tails behind. Rated DC30V 0.5A, 5000 cycles, PBT / brass-Ni / BeCu-Ag. *** PINOUT, cross-checked two ways (drawing schematic, and a KiCad footprint whose pads are NAMED with offsets matching the drawing's 4.92 / 3.38 / 6.48): PIN 3 = TIP, PIN 2 = TIP-NORMAL SWITCH CONTACT - NORMALLY CLOSED TO PIN 3 AND OPENING WHEN A PLUG IS INSERTED - PIN 1 = SLEEVE. *** All three on one centreline, oval drill 1.6 x 0.6. LEAVE A 3mm HOLE OR A VOID IN THE PCB UNDER THE BARREL (Thonk's own note). THE SWITCH CONTACT IS FREE NORMALLING and nothing in the design uses it yet - worth knowing before the layout rather than after. description: Umbilical cable, module to instrument

A stranded Cat5e PATCH lead is commonly 26 or 28 AWG, at 1.6x to 2.6x the resistance. WHAT DECIDES IT: buy the lead, read the jacket print, or measure end-to-end DC resistance at E6. STRANDED not solid-core: solid core work-hardens and fractures under constant flexing, which is this cable's whole life. A SHIELD BUYS NOTHING HERE: neither etherCON terminates it (their G tabs are on no net, ADR 0027 'What it is not'), so UTP and STP serve alike.
